text:
anita: quick follow-up from the autoscale sync — I want to propose a two-tier model for Dedicated GPU pools: steady-state lanes (reserved, predictable) + burst lanes (ephemeral, admission-controlled). sketching tradeoffs and an interface.

samir: sounds promising. how do you see admission control interacting with per-customer priority/committed capacity?

anita: idea: admission control checks (1) steady quota, (2) burst budget token, (3) SLO priority. burst tokens refilled per-minute and can be borrowed across customers with weighting. if no tokens -> enqueue or 429.

leah: curious about cold starts for burst lanes — we can't afford large latency spikes for chat customers. any prewarm plan?

anita: yes — small prewarm pool per-region that holds N prewarmed processes per popular model. admission control gives preference to requests matching prewarm signature. prewarm config example:

```
PoolPrewarm:
  model: gpt-redwood-xxx
  count: 2
  ttl_minutes: 10
```

michael: eviction and graceful drain are key. we need KV cache snapshot/transfer or allow cold-resume. proposal: when evicting, mark sessions as migrating, accept only short tail tokens, and stream KV to next node async; fallback to cold resume after grace period.

ryan: cost side — burst lanes must have a hard cost cap per-customer and global burst budget. if usage approaches cap, admission control toggles stricter policies (batching required, quantized variants, or client fallback).

anita: exactly. also adding an API hook for Console to show per-route burst spend and token balance, plus alerts when borrow-rate > threshold.

samir: interface boundary question — should the admission controller live in the per-region runtime or as a central controller? tradeoffs?

anita: central controller easier for global budgets and consistent borrowing logic, but adds extra network hop and single point of failure. regional controller reduces latency and works with local prewarms but needs eventual-consistency replication of budgets. leaning to a hybrid: regionally-enforced fast path + eventual central arbiter for long-lived rebalancing.

leah: can we express policies declaratively? would help ops and customers.

anita: yes. example policy DSL (very rough):

```
policy {
  customer: premium
  burst: {
    max_nodes: 8
    refill: 60s
    rules: ["prefer-prewarm","allow-quantized" ]
  }
}
```

michael: metrics we need: admission_rejects, borrowed_tokens, prewarm_hit_rate, avg_cold_latency, cost_per_token_burst. add rollup to Console.

ryan: +1 to including fallback models in policy. for large customers we can auto-route to cheaper quantized variant when burst budget low.

anita: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC covering: interface (policy DSL + API), admission controller placement (hybrid), prewarm sizing heuristics, eviction protocol, metrics + Console hooks, and cost safety knobs. comments welcome.

samir: please include sequence diagrams for request flow and failure modes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy pipeline note — please tag rfc-[eng-runtime] in PR for visibility to eng-infra.

leah: thanks — will review once RFC lands.

anita: thanks all — aiming to post RFC by EOD Friday.
